questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The policeman / walk along the / road when I saw / a body in the gutter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **walk along the** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The error lies in the part **“walk along the”.**
 
• From the given sentence it is clear that it is a past incident.
 
• In past tense, the verb must be in past tense.
 
• **‘walk’ **is present tense(V1). So, we need the verb "**walk**" to be in the past continuous (also called past progressive) tense as it suggests an ongoing action in the past.
 
• The past continuous consists of two elements: the past tense of the verb **"to be"** (was/were), and the base **verb +ing.**
 
• By changing "**walk**" to "**was walking**," the two verbs in the sentence both indicate past events.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is* "The policeman **was walking **along the road when I saw a body in the gutter."*

*​*Hence,** option 1** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• If we change '**saw' **into '**see'**, the part **"walk along the"** will still remain incorrect. Because the subject "The policeman" is a singular subject.
 
• **"The police" **is a plural subject.
 
• The choice between singular and plural depends on whether the focus is on an individual officer or the collective actions of the entire police force.
